newsitem.title: UK: INSIGHT - Sterling to drift to 2.7660 marks prop.
newsitem.headline: INSIGHT - Sterling to drift to 2.7660 marks prop.

text.p: Sterling has retreated back into a familiar range after advancing to 2.8055 marks on Monday, and is now set to drift lower on the day, chartists said.
The pound is expected to find support around 2.7730-7660, in the middle of its established trading range, ahead of 2.7450 and then its four-month uptrend at 2.7255.
"We've failed at interim resistance and we're likely to come back and test support around 2.7660," said Karen Jones, technical analyst at Credit Suisse First Boston in London.
The key upside level for sterling to recapture is now around 2.8080 marks, Jones said.

The 2.8080 area represents a 78.6 percent Fibonacci retracement of the pound's recent upmove from the May 12 low of 2.7240 marks to yesterday's high of 2.8055. Above 2.8080 sets sterling on course for 2.8330-65, Jones said.
The pound stood at 2.7830/40 marks at 0742 GMT, down from 2.8000/10 here late Monday, tracking a decline in dollar/mark.

"With the dollar weak on the day it's a likely scenario that we drift back down. We should now hold below 2.7950," said Eddie Matts, director at Capital Management. "I think we've seen the top above 2.80 and we pull back initially to the 2.77 region and then break down again."
Cable capitalised on the dollar's weakness, pushing to $1.6493/98 by 0746 GMT from Monday's Europe close of $1.6368/73.

Analysts saw the next major obstacle at $1.6550, which was the April 1 peak and a 50 percent retracement of sterling's decline from the December 31 high of $1.7163 to this year's low of $1.5850, hit on March 18.
"Today we're looking for $1.64 to hold as cable spikes up to $1.6550. That should cause a bounce, but I suspect it may spike to $1.6550 before it's able to turn around," said Matts.
